no_duplicated_code.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Duplicated Code smell?

criteria.pass: Domain rules, validation checks, error mappings, and persistence or transformation blocks are factored cleanly without copy-pasted logic across functions, branches, or files.
criteria.fail: Substantially similar validation logic, business rules, control-flow blocks, or query/mapping fragments are copy-pasted in multiple places instead of being unified into a shared helper or owning domain method.

no_long_functions.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Long Function smell, judging each individual function, method, or callback by its own inline executable logic?

criteria.pass: Each executable function, method, or callback stays concise and focused on a cohesive level of abstraction, delegating substantial implementation mechanics to well-named helpers, collaborators, or domain methods. Cohesive workflow, boundary, transaction, streaming, and orchestration functions (including concise transaction or resource-scoped callbacks) pass when they sequence calls to named helpers or collaborators with clear step ordering. Do not fail solely for overall file or class size, supporting type or interface declarations, declarative UI or markup composition, formatting or static literals, or an enclosing container that defines multiple short, independently triggered handlers or lifecycle callbacks.
criteria.fail: One or more individual executable functions, methods, or callbacks are long monolithic bodies that implement multiple substantial processing phases inline (such as writing out parsing, validation rules, policy calculations, state mutations, retry or I/O loops, and persistence or output formatting directly inside one function) where extracting named helpers is warranted to clarify intent and reduce nesting. A concise coordinator that sequences calls to named helpers or collaborators—even across several workflow steps or inside a short transaction callback—does NOT fail.

no_long_parameter_lists_or_data_clumps.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of Long Parameter List and Data Clumps smells?

criteria.pass: Function and constructor parameter lists stay concise (typically up to 4 distinct parameters, or a structured options/input object when more inputs are needed), and groups of values that naturally belong together (such as start/end dates, ranges, or request inputs) are grouped into cohesive domain or boundary types rather than passed repeatedly as separate primitives.
criteria.fail: Functions take sprawling parameter lists (such as 5+ loose primitive parameters that belong in an input object), or the same cluster of primitive values is repeatedly passed together across multiple method signatures instead of being modeled as a cohesive value object.

no_feature_envy_or_data_class_anemia.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of Feature Envy and anemic Data Class smells?

criteria.pass: Domain behavior, invariant checks, policy rules, and state transitions live with the domain types that own the relevant data rather than being computed externally. Boundary request/response DTOs and thin persistence row mappers may remain simple data carriers.
criteria.fail: Service, controller, or helper methods repeatedly pull fields out of passive domain data classes to compute rules, policies, or state transitions that belong on the owning domain type.

no_message_chains.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Message Chains smell?

criteria.pass: Callers interact directly with their collaborators or intention-revealing domain methods rather than navigating deep chains of nested object properties to reach internal data. Fluent builders, standard library collection pipelines, framework/DB query chains, and shallow property reads on nested document/value structs (such as `record.section.field`) are acceptable.
criteria.fail: Code repeatedly navigates deep object-graph property chains (such as reaching through multiple nested domain objects to inspect or manipulate internal fields) instead of asking the owning object directly.

no_primitive_obsession.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Primitive Obsession smell, flagging only visibly unconstrained primitives rather than imported domain types or standard protocol/UI values?

criteria.pass: Constrained domain concepts, structured value groups, and shared semantic thresholds use dedicated types, unions/enums, or named constants rather than visibly unconstrained primitives, untyped tuples, or coupled behavioral boolean flag clusters. Literal comparisons against values typed by a named local or imported domain type (including fields or properties of imported domain types), union/enum, constant collection, or validation schema are NOT raw magic-string defects—treat imported domain types and their fields as properly constrained when their declarations live outside the supplied file. Standard protocol, HTTP, markup/DOM, and parser fields/literals/status codes, independent UI or view-state flags, ordinary arithmetic and counts, timestamps/ISO strings, opaque IDs, tokens/hashes, and boundary/storage DTO fields remain acceptable as plain primitives unless an unmodeled domain invariant requires wrapping.
criteria.fail: The supplied code visibly declares a constrained domain concept, state set, unit, or multi-field structure using unconstrained raw primitive types, untyped pairs/tuples, or coupled behavioral boolean control flags, OR repeats raw magic strings or unnamed domain thresholds/sentinels on unconstrained primitives where a shared named constant, union/enum, or value type belongs. Comparing values typed by an imported or local domain type (or its fields) against literal members, or using plain primitives for standard protocol/HTTP fields and status codes, opaque IDs, ordinary counts, or independent UI state flags, does NOT fail.

no_repeated_switches.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of the Repeated Switches smell?

criteria.pass: Conditional dispatch on a domain type, tier, or status is consolidated onto the owning enum/sealed hierarchy or a single authoritative location rather than repeated across multiple functions or classes.
criteria.fail: Multiple `when`/`if` chains across different methods or files branch on the same enum, status, or tier discriminator to implement scattered variant-specific rules.

no_speculative_or_middle_man.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of Speculative Generality, Lazy Element, and Middle Man smells?

criteria.pass: Every class, interface, and wrapper earns its keep with a concrete responsibility required by the task, without unused extension points, speculative abstractions, or trivial pass-through delegates.
criteria.fail: The code contains speculative interfaces/abstractions for hypothetical future needs, near-empty types with no real responsibility, or middle-man classes whose methods merely forward calls unchanged to another object.

no_comment_deodorant_or_dead_code.instructions: Is the supplied production code free of Comments-as-Deodorant and Dead Code smells?

criteria.pass: Comments are reserved for non-obvious rationale, concurrency/locking intent, or contract nuances rather than narrating obvious lines or apologizing for convoluted code, and there is no commented-out code or unreachable private dead code.
criteria.fail: The code contains noisy comments that merely restate obvious code, comments excusing unclear logic that should be refactored, commented-out code blocks, or unused private helpers/constants.
